fields.v: Feeder slides/rolls balls along the table surface toward your wing. Normal ready position.
Knees low, racket below table level, brush up the back of the rolling ball with an accelerating low-to-high swing. Visible arc, lands on the table. Alternate FH and BH sets.
3 × 20 balls forehand + 3 × 20 balls backhand. Session opener, or after any technical change.
Foundation: near-still ball, land 10 in a row anywhere · Competitor: rolling ball, deep half · Advanced: faster feed, alternate wings every ball, deep corners.
10 rolled balls per wing — clean deep topspins. 8/10 = move up.
Knees before arm. Contact thin as paper. Finish above head height.
Multiball. Feeder alternates: one short backspin ball to your backhand, one long ball to your backhand.
Step in with the right foot, flick with wrist over the top — push back out to distance — drop the racket and topspin the long ball with the full stroke. Fixed target first (their deep backhand).
6–10 series of 8 balls (4 pairs), 30–45 s rest.
Foundation: announced pattern, slow rhythm · Competitor: match rhythm, fixed target · Advanced: feeder randomly doubles one of the two.
10 balls (5 pairs): pairs where BOTH shots land. 4/5 = move up.
In-and-out with the feet, not by leaning. Flick = wrist and forearm; topspin = legs and hip. Never let them blend.
Multiball. One short backspin ball to your forehand, one long ball to your forehand.
Step in deep with the right foot, flick with a stable wrist (guide, don't whip) — push off that same foot to recover — unload a full forehand topspin on the long ball.
6–10 series of 8 balls, 30–45 s rest.
As D2. Advanced: the long ball comes faster and sometimes into the elbow — recovery includes a sideways adjustment.
5 pairs: 4/5 with both shots clean = move up.
The push back OUT of the table is the whole drill. Late on the long ball = the mistake happened at the recovery step.
Multiball, medium pace. Ball 1 to your BH corner, ball 2 to the middle, ball 3 toward the FH side — ALL played with the backhand. Repeat.
Small side-steps between every ball, shoulders square to each contact point. One fixed deep target until stable, then feeder calls targets.
6–8 series of 9 balls (3 rounds of the 3 points).
Foundation: 2 points, slower · Competitor: 3 points, fixed target · Advanced: random order of the three points.
9 balls in sequence: 8/9 on the table with real spin = move up.
Arrive, then swing — never swing while sliding. The feet change; the backhand does not.
Multiball. Ball 1 to your FH corner, ball 2 middle, ball 3 into your BH corner — ALL with the forehand. Repeat.
Two small steps, then one big cross-step into the backhand corner for ball 3. Hips fully rotate on every ball. Fixed deep target (elbow or deep middle) until stable.
6–8 series of 9 balls. It burns the legs — that is the point.
Foundation: 2 points · Competitor: 3 in order · Advanced: random order, ball 3 occasionally faster.
8/9 in sequence = move up.
On the pivot, right foot BEHIND the ball line. A balanced 80% forehand scores more than a falling 100% one.
Multiball or a blocking partner. Ball 1 to your backhand (BH), ball 2 to your backhand again (pivot, FH), ball 3 wide to your forehand (cross-step, FH).
Continuous series at a rhythm you can barely sustain with quality. Fixed target first.
6–10 series of 9–12 balls.
Foundation: slow, smaller distances · Competitor: match rhythm · Advanced: partner blocks live — the rhythm breathes like a rally.
9 balls: 8/9 clean = move up.
The cross-step to the wide forehand starts BEFORE your pivot forehand has landed. Trust the pattern.
Pattern drills are predictable; matches are not. D7 restores read-and-react while keeping multiball's density.
Multiball anywhere — any lane, any depth, any spin — at 10–15% below your maximum rhythm.
Attack every long ball, touch or flick every short ball, neutral ready position between contacts. No stroke thoughts — only the feeder's racket.
4–6 series of 45–60 s, at the END of a technical session, when tired — the 9–9-in-the- fifth state.
Foundation: two lanes, one depth · Competitor: full table, two depths · Advanced: all depths, broken rhythm.
60-second series: fewer than 4 unforced errors = move up.
Eyes on the feeder's contact, not the last ball you hit. The earlier you see it, the slower the game feels.
The bridge from drills to matches; the daily rehearsal of Combinations A and B. Serve → forced return → first attack is the most common point-winning structure in the sport.

Live with a partner. You serve with full intention; partner returns (agreed return at Foundation, freely at higher levels); the point plays out — but only serve, return and third ball are scored in your head.
Blocks of 10 serves per pattern. A: short backspin to their FH → topspin wide BH. B: short to their BH → topspin wide FH. Also: fast long to the elbow → counter the block.
3–4 blocks of 10 serves, 2–3 × per week, all year. Swap roles — your partner trains receive.
Foundation: partner pushes every return long · Competitor: free returns · Advanced: partner actively punishes your serve.
10 serves of a banker pattern: third-ball attacks launched as planned. Target: 10/10.
Serve with a plan, never to 'start the point'. Before every serve, know where the return goes and what you do with it.

fields.v: Live. Serve short backspin; both keep the rally short with touch pushes (every ball would bounce twice). Base version: partner deliberately pushes long to the MIDDLE after 2–4 short balls.
The instant a push comes long — full topspin, spin-first, deep. Pushing a long ball back = point lost by rule. Swap roles every 10 balls.
3–4 blocks of 10 openings per player, 2–3 × per week.
Foundation: long push always to the middle, agreed ball · Competitor: random timing, middle or BH · Advanced: free short game with flicks; FIRST long ball must be attacked.
10 long pushes offered: openings launched with real spin. 8/10 = move up.
Decide 'short or long' before the ball crosses the net. Stay low, weight forward — from a tall stance every push looks short.
Partner blocks a fixed loop: (1) BH corner — backhand · (2) middle — forehand · (3) BH corner — backhand · (4) FH side — forehand. Repeat continuously.
5 minutes, as many quality repetitions as possible. Then swap with your partner.
Wakes the BH–FH transition and the middle ball taken with the forehand — the ball that decides more league rallies than any corner.
Every ball off a real step. None from a standstill.
(1) FH side — forehand · (2) middle — forehand · (3) FH side — forehand · (4) BH corner — backhand. Repeat continuously.
5 minutes, maximum clean repetitions.
After W1 + W2 the forehand has fired from all three zones and the backhand from two — before the match starts.
Rhythm over power. This is activation, not a highlight reel.
Both players behind the table trading FOREHAND counter-topspins. Start offset: you on your BH side (FH from the corner), partner on his FH side — the rally travels down one straight line.
Every ball, both drift one small step sideways in the same direction. After 5–7 balls positions are fully swapped — then drift back.
5 minutes.
Rehearses the mid-distance counter-loop — the stroke that decides open rallies — from every angle, with live feet.
Slow, high-spin balls. The drill is the feet and the feel, not the winner.
Stable bench or plyo box (30–40 cm), 2–3 m behind the table. Feeder ready.
One multiball series (any of D2–D6, 8–12 balls) → jump BACKWARD onto the bench → down the far side → jump up again → down on the table side → straight into the next series.
6–10 rounds. Rest only while the feeder gathers balls.
Foundation: step up, lower bench, 4–6 rounds · Competitor: as written · Advanced: two over-and-backs, or hold a light med ball.
Land soft and silent, knees over toes, eyes forward. Loud landings or caving knees = stop the circuit.
Standard court space (~14 × 7 m). Feeder ready.
Multiball series → on the last ball sprint to the back barrier, touch it, run back, hit the ready position — feeder starts the next series the moment you arrive.
6–10 rounds, or alternate P1 and P2 rounds for the complete circuit.
Foundation: jog, feeder waits 3 s · Competitor: as written · Advanced: return BACKWARD-facing on alternate rounds.
The sprint is not the test — the FIRST BALL of the next series is.
Flat ladder, 4–6 m. Before table training or inside a physical session.
(A) two feet per box, forward, max frequency · (B) lateral in-in/out-out, both directions · (C) icky shuffle · (D) crossover run. Quality first, speed second, always both directions.
2 runs of each pattern per direction, 20–30 s rest. 8–10 min total.
Foundation: A + B at half speed · Competitor: all four at speed · Advanced: finish every run with a split-step + shadow forehand.
Balls of the feet, sprinter arms. If the pattern breaks, slow down — the nervous system learns what you repeat, including mistakes.
Racket in hand, mirror or table. Optional cones at the corners of your zone.

30–45 s blocks with FULL stroke shadows: (1) side-to-side FH–BH · (2) Falkenberg pattern · (3) in-and-out (shadow flick in, shadow topspin out) · (4) free shadow play against an imagined opponent (doubles as visualization).
6–10 blocks, 30 s rest. Warm-up, home workout, or session finisher.
Foundation: patterns 1–2, moderate rhythm · Competitor: all at match rhythm · Advanced: light resistance blocks, then always free-speed to finish.
Full strokes, real balance, imaginary ball watched with real eyes. Lazy shadows teach lazy strokes.
Solid wall or partner, 2–4 kg ball. Fresh, after warm-up — power is never junk volume.

(1) rotational side throw, both sides — load the back hip, release at hip height like a forehand · (2) overhead slam · (3) explosive chest pass · (4) low-to-high diagonal 'topspin throw', both sides. Maximum intent every rep.
3–4 sets × 6–8 reps per throw, full rest 60–90 s. In-season 1–2×/week, off-season 2– 3×.
Foundation: 2 kg, throws 1 + 3 · Competitor: 3 kg, all four · Advanced: 4 kg + 5 max-speed shadow strokes after each set (contrast training).
Throw with the hips, finish with the hands.

(1) back/goblet squat 4×6 · (2) Bulgarian split squat 3×8/leg · (3) Romanian deadlift 3×8 · (4) one-arm row 3×10/arm · (5) half-kneeling press 3×8/arm · (6) core: Pallof press 3×10/side, side plank 3×30 s/side, dead bug 3×10.
Competitor level up: after each squat set — 5 maximal jumps; after split squats — 5 lateral bounds per side.
Off-season 2–3×/week (the main event) · in-season 1×/week, moderate loads, never the day before a match. 45–60 min.
Foundation: bodyweight/goblet, learn movements · Competitor: loaded + jump pairings · Advanced: periodized with a professional.
Anti-rotation core beats endless sit-ups — a rotation sport needs brakes as much as an engine. Technique is non-negotiable.
